plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare, dark branches come alive with small, spicy-sweet blossoms in blush pink, rose and white. The flowers open before the leaves, and their perfume drifts across gardens and shrines while the air is still cold. Visitors flock to ume groves to see them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring, usually January through March, with peak bloom in February and early March
plants.location: Japan, where ume groves and plum festivals are at their best in late February
plants.funFact: Ume flowers open weeks before cherry blossoms. In East Asia they are a symbol of perseverance and the first hint of spring. The same trees produce the sour fruit used for umeboshi pickles and plum wine.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.commonName: Agapanthus (African lily, lily of the Nile)
plants.description: Tall, bare stems hold round clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers in blue and violet. They rise above arching, strap-like leaves like fireworks frozen in midair. Councils plant them along streets and in public gardens, where they bloom through the summer months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, which in the Southern Hemisphere runs from December to February
plants.location: Australia, in gardens and public plantings, where late February is the end of the summer flowering season
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, agapanthus is not a true lily. It is native to southern Africa, and its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'. It is so hardy that it has escaped from Australian gardens and now grows wild in some bushland.
